title: Region drain tagging race caused tier swap and cascading fallback surge
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-03-01 a mis-coordinated region drain propagation caused the smart router to mark a healthy EU-west cluster as draining for a subset of routes. This triggered a tier-based routing swap that pushed traffic to lower-capacity Dedicated pools and then into fallback model variants in multiple regions, producing elevated latency, increased token costs, and a transient error spike for ~55 minutes. This ticket records the postmortem, immediate mitigations, and follow-up action items.
timeline: 2026-03-01T09:02Z - Automated maintenance job started to decommission a small EU-west rack (scheduled).
2026-03-01T09:06Z - Drain job wrote tombstone tags to the cluster metadata store but the propagation to the routing cache was delayed due to a transient watcher lag (internal watcher queue spike).

2026-03-01T09:07Z - Routing controller saw partial drain state for subset of hosts and evaluated tier policies: affected routes were configured to prefer low-latency region + tier affinity. Controller decided to failover to next-tier targets (Dedicated burst pool in EU-central).

2026-03-01T09:08Z - Dedicated pool neared capacity; smart router initiated fallback to lower-memory model variants in US-west and EU-central to preserve latency SLOs (automatic variant fallback enabled).

2026-03-01T09:10Z - Fallback cascade: requests routed across mixed variants caused increased KV cache misses and token amplification, further increasing load and triggering additional fallback steps and retries between 09:10Z-09:45Z.
2026-03-01T09:23Z - Error rates rose to 6.4% on affected routes; median latency increased from 120ms to 760ms for impacted customer subset.

2026-03-01T09:30Z - On-call noticed alerts (routing-error surge dashboard) and manually applied emergency routing override to pin critical customers to their dedicated host groups, bypassing the stale drain state.
2026-03-01T09:40Z - Drain job was rolled back; watcher queue cleared and routing cache refreshed. Normal routing gradually resumed between 09:42Z-09:58Z.
2026-03-01T10:00Z - Incident declared resolved; postmortem investigation kicked off.
2026-03-05T12:00Z - Postmortem review completed with cross-team attendance (routing, serving runtime, infra, SRE, product).
impact_summary: Approximately 14% of production routes experienced degraded performance for ~55 minutes. Estimated customer-facing errors affected 120 active API keys; two customers reported timeouts and one reported model-quality regressions due to variant swaps. Estimated incremental token cost during incident: ~18% for affected workloads.
root_cause: A race between the drain automation (which writes tombstones into the cluster metadata store) and the routing controller's cache update mechanism. The drain job wrote partial tombstones with an inconsistent tombstone TTL and due to a watcher queue lag the routing cache observed a partially applied drain state. The controller's tier routing logic treated the partial drain as a hard decommission signal for some hosts, triggering a tier swap. Automatic variant fallback logic, which reacts to capacity signals and latency, then amplified the effect because it lacked a short-circuit check for multi-region simultaneous variant churn.
contributing_factors: Drain automation writes tombstones in two steps without a transactional marker — susceptible to intermediate visibility.
Routing cache watcher backpressure: watcher queue has no backpressure mitigation and can stall updates for ~30-60s under control-plane load.
Tier routing policy is aggressive: treats partial drain signals as full host removal for certain latency-sensitive routes.
Variant fallback path has no circuit-breaker for cascading fallbacks across regions; it reacts only to local capacity signals.
Insufficient synthetic traffic checks for cross-region variant consistency leading to delayed detection.
detection_and_response: Detection: routing-error surge dashboard alerted SRE at 09:23Z (custom alert threshold hit for error rate and token amplification), and on-call saw correlated latency increase on top routes.
Initial response: SRE paged routing/serving leads, throttled non-critical background traffic and applied emergency routing override to pin critical customers to origin host pools.
Rollback: operator rolled back the drain job at 09:40Z and forced routing cache refresh across control-plane instances.
Post-incident: full timeline reconstructed, relevant logs and traces archived to incident folder and metrics snapshots captured for regression testing.
mitigations_applied: Emergency routing override to pin critical API keys to stable host assignments (manual).
Rollback of the maintenance drain job to stop further tombstone writes.
Forcible routing-cache refresh and restart of watcher service on two control-plane instances to clear stale state.
Temporary throttle put on automatic variant fallback for affected regions for 1 hour to prevent re-triggering cascade.
long_term_actions: ENG-1: Convert drain automation to a two-phase commit with an explicit 'drain-ready' marker; ensure routing controller treats only completed drains as hard removals. Owner: Priya Rao - due 2026-03-26.
ENG-2: Add watcher backpressure handling and sliding-window health for routing cache updates to avoid 30-60s stalls. Owner: Rafael Kim - due 2026-04-02.
ENG-3: Update tier routing policy to delay hard tier swaps until a confirmation window (e.g., 20s) and add a 'soft-drain' state for transient visibility. Owner: Liam O'Rourke - due 2026-03-19.
ENG-4: Implement cross-region fallback circuit breaker that prevents multi-region variant churn within a configurable cooldown. Owner: Maya Patel - due 2026-04-09.
ENG-5: Add synthetic canary flows that exercise variant fallbacks across regions and surface inconsistencies to the routing-error dashboard. Owner: SRE Team - due 2026-03-30.
ENG-6: Create automated regression tests in the routing simulator to replay partial tombstone visibility and assert no cascading fallbacks. Owner: Routing Team - due 2026-04-16.
owners_and_due_dates: Priya Rao - Convert drain automation to 2PC - 2026-03-26
Rafael Kim - Watcher backpressure and cache resilience - 2026-04-02
Liam O'Rourke - Tier routing confirmation window - 2026-03-19
SRE Team (oncall rotation) - Canary flows and dashboards - 2026-03-30
notes: This incident exposes a common class of race (partial metadata visibility) between control-plane writers and cache consumers; routing logic must be conservative.
We chose to classify as P0 because of customer-visible errors and cost amplification.
Follow-ups should be tracked as discrete engineering tasks (ENG-1..ENG-6 above) and reported in the next reliability review.
